specials.description: Wights may gain experience, however Wights promoted to become Heroes by rolling The lad's got talent will be unable to search for rare items in the same way as Grave Guards. They must choose the Combat and Strength skill lists if promoted. Wights also gain Wight Blades if they become Heroes.

fighters.name: Scarecrow
fighters.fixed_kit: The scarecrow carries no equipment and suffers no penalties for this.

specials.name: No Pain (Scarecrow)
specials.description: The scarecrow treats all stunned results on the injury chart as knocked down.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Zombies never gain experience.

specials.name: No Substance
specials.description: The scarecrow is incredibly difficult to take down with shooting as there are few vital parts to hit. The scarecrow counts as having a T6 against all shooting and magical missiles, likewise, a scarecrow is immune to critical hits caused by shooting. The exception to this rule is missile weapons or spells that are fire based which deal damage as normal.

specials.name: Flammable
specials.description: The scarecrow is primarily ratty cloth, straw and preserved body parts so as a result they burn very easily. Scarecrows count as being flammable. In addition, a scarecrow will be 'caught fire' on the roll of a 3+ as opposed to the normal 4+.

specials.name: Construct
specials.description: The scarecrow is an undead construct and may re-roll any rolls on the injury table except for wounds caused by fire.

specials.name: Animated Construct
specials.description:
Powerful constructs such as scarecrows require much more concentration from their summoners than normal skeletons or zombies to remain animated. The scarecrow is controlled by either the Liche or the Necromancer (note down on the warband roster which), but each may only control one at a time, so only a warband with both a Liche and a Necromancer may ever take two Scarecrows. If the Liche or the Necromancer is for some reason unable to participate in a battle, their Scarecrow will also be unable to participate.

Whenever the scarecrow's controller loses a wound he must pass an unmodified Leadership test or the magical bond is broken and the scarecrow is immediately taken out of action.

rules.title: Hard Head
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs and Bull Centaurs ignore the special rules for maces, clubs, etc. They are not easy to knock out!

rules.title: Armour
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs and Bull Centaurs never suffer movement penalties for wearing armour.

rules.title: Hard to Kill
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs and Bull Centaurs are tough, resilient individuals who can only be taken out of action on a roll of 6 instead of 5-6 when rolling on the Injury chart. Treat a roll of 1-2 as knocked down, 3-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.

rules.title: Slavers
rules.description:
One of the main objectives of the Chaos Dwarfs of Mordheim is to get more slaves for their sacrifices and for their tasks. Consequently, the Chaos Dwarfs will never free any slave they capture.

Pick one: Sacrifice them or put them to work. If you sacrifice them, the apprentice sorcerer will get +1 to Experience for each slave sacrificed. If put to work, you force them to help them in their quest for the witchstone; at the end of the game, gain an additional +1 wyrdstone for each working slave; then make a 1D6 roll: On a result of 2 to 6, the captive dies due to overwork, disease, the effects of long exposure to the sorcerer’s stone, or for any other similar reason, and the Chaos Dwarf band may keep the captive’s equipment. On a result of 1, the captive manages to escape, returns to his band with his equipment intact and, in addition, gains an experience bonus of 1D3 (if he is a henchman, simply add 1 to his total).

rules.title: Uncommon
rules.description: Chaos Dwarfs are quite rare in Old World settlements. For this reason, when they make rolls for the acquisition of new recruits in their bands, they have to spend 1.5 times (rounding up) the amount of experience they normally spend for veterancy. Remember that this is not the case for Hobgoblins, a race far more common than that of Chaos Dwarfs. For example, a group of Chaos Dwarf recruits armed with blunderbusses with 4 experience points would require at least 6 experience points to acquire one recruit, 12 to recruit two and so on.

rules.title: Indentured Servants
rules.description: A Chaos Dwarf warband must start with at least 4 Hobgoblins; if it drops below 4 Hobgoblins, you cannot recruit other members until the number of Hobgoblins is increased to four or more.

rules.title: Hired Swords
rules.description: A Chaos Dwarf warband may hire the following Hired Swords: Ogre Bodyguard, Pit Fighter, Warlock, Imperial Assassin, and Hobgoblin Scout. They may hire any Hired Sword described as “all may hire,” or allowed by Orc warbands and Chaos warbands. They may never hire Elves of any sort!

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6“ of the Apprentice Sorcerer may use his Leadership when taking Ld tests.

specials.name: Rituals of Chaos
specials.description: Chaos Dwarf spellcasters are wizards and can learn a random spell from the Chaos Dwarf spell list.

specials.name: Skinny
specials.description: Hobgoblins are naturally cowardly creatures that are forced to fight by their Chaos Dwarf masters. As a result, they take damage easily and at the slightest opportunity try to escape from their captors. When making serious injury rolls, a result of 1-3 indicates that they abandon the band.

specials.name: Nobody cares about them
specials.description: Hobgoblins count as half the number of troops if the band has to make a rout check. For example, in a band made of 12 miniatures, if 2 Hobgoblin miniatures and 1 Chaos Dwarf miniature are out of action, the total would be two miniatures out of action (1/2 + 1/2 +1 =2). Also, Hobgoblins cannot be heroes, just reroll the “Lad's got talent” roll.

rules.title: Miragliano
rules.description:
Therefore Miraglean Heroes have a +1 to hit when using crossbows only.

Marksmen get a +1 to hit with any missile weapon they use.

All Miragleans have a deep-seated hatred toward Skaven. This dates back to the red pox outbreak of 1812 when three quarters of the population of the city perished. When fighting Skaven a Miraglean warband will be affected by the rules for hatred towards them. Hired swords are not affected by the Hatred rule.

Hired Swords: Miragleans warband cannot have Skaven Hired Swords.

rules.title: Remas
rules.description:
To represent this, the Remasen player is allowed to re-roll any rout test one time and must abide by the second roll. This only applies when fighting Dark Elves.

Remasen officers are steadfast individuals whose years of training have afforded them excellent leadership. The leadership value of a Remasen captain, champion and young blood are always one point higher regardless of whom they are fighting.

Hired Swords: Remasens warband cannot have Dark Elf Hired Swords.

rules.title: Trantio
rules.description: To represent this a Trantio war band will always start a one-off match with an extra 100 GC and in a Lustrian campaign they will start with an extra 20% GC added to their total.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: Any warrior within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership characteristic when taking Leadership tests.

specials.name: Cloak & Dagger
specials.description: Duellists are adept at fighting using their billowing cloaks to swirl at an enemy distracting him and warding off blows. The Duellist counts as using a buckler in close combat.

rules.title: Cause Fear
rules.description: All Undead warriors cause Fear.

rules.title: Immune to Psychology
rules.description: All Undead warriors are immune to psychology and never leave combat.

rules.title: No pain
rules.description: All Undead warriors treat a Stunned result as Knocked Down.

rules.title: May not run
rules.description: No Undead warrior may run, but may charge as normal.

rules.title: Immune to poison
rules.description: No Undead warrior is affected by poison.

rules.title: No Brain
rules.description:
Skeletons are not alive, thus they never gain experience.

Note: Tomb Lords don't actually learn new skills, rather they remember the skills they knew when they were alive. Liche Priests and Acolyes are also undead but the have retained a form of living mind and are capable of learning from their experiences.

rules.title: Flammable
rules.description: The Tomb Lord is as dry as tinder and wrapped in bandages soaked in highly flammable resins and preservatives. A hit from a fire-based attack will cause double the normal number of wounds on it.

rules.title: Do not Drink
rules.description: Undead models do not need food and water. However any living animals that accompany the Mummies follow the water rules as normal.

rules.title: Home Ground
rules.description: The Tomb Guardians live in the Necropolises and have no trouble locating the hidden tombs in search of weapons and armour to help them defend their homes. A Tomb Guardian warband always roll one extra dice in the Exploration phase.

specials.name: Leader
specials.description: The Tomb Lord is the warband's Leader and follows all the rules for Leaders.

specials.name: Undead
specials.description: The Tomb Lord is undead and follows all rules for the Undead.

specials.description: Skeletons are undead and follow all rules for the Undead.

specials.name: Undead (Tomb Guardian)
specials.description: The Tomb Guards are undead and follow all rules for the Undead.

fighters.name: Tomb Scorpion
fighters.fixed_kit: Scorpions don't use weapons or armour.

specials.name: Living
specials.description: Scorpions are living beings and are affected by Psychology as normal. However as they are small desert creatures they do not need water.

specials.name: Animals
specials.description: Scorpions are animals and do not gain experience points.

specials.name: Scorpions sting*
specials.description: Scorpions attack using the poisonous sting in their tails. This attack is worked out exactly as if the scorpion was attacking with Black Lotus.

specials.description: Dire Wolves do not gain experience. You can’t teach an old dog new tricks!

specials.description: Zombies treat a stunned result on the Injury chart as knocked down.

specials.name: No Brain
specials.description: Zombies never gain experience. They do not learn from their mistakes. What did you expect?

lists.note: This list is for Flagellants only.

specials.description: The Warrior-Priest is a servant of Sigmar and may use the Prayers of Sigmar as detailed in the Magic section and the Warrior-Priest start with one prayer generated at random. In addition the Warrior-Priest may learn a new Prayer instead of a new skill.

specials.name: Fanatical
specials.description: Flagellants are convinced that the end of the world is nigh, and nothing in this world holds any terror for them. Flagellants automatically pass all Leadership-based tests they are required to take. A Flagellant may never become a warband leader.

fighters.name: War hounds
fighters.fixed_kit: Jaws and brutality! War hounds never use or need weapons and armour.
